repo_prior_art.cite: none; the only completed panel catalogue entry is panel_ppml_forbidden_comparison, which concerns PPML forbidden comparisons rather than PT--SC union efficiency.

published_prior_art.cite: SunXieZhang2025 gives ATT identification and branchwise PT/SC asymptotics; TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 gives intersection efficiency for a different odds-ratio union model, not a PT--SC ATT union convolution bound.
No cited paper gives this PT--SC equality condition, but its stated iff is largely the Hilbert-space projection consequence of Theorem 1 rather than an independently developed observable frontier.
SunXieZhang2025 and ChenSantAnnaXie2025 do not exhibit a nondegenerate PT--SC intersection region with distinct canonical gradients and a strict union-efficiency cost.
SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the established two-group panel-DiD efficiency result; the reduction is a useful calibration consequence, not a new standalone result.
SunXieZhang2025 proves branch-specific inference, while NeweyRobins2018 and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 do not treat an estimated PT--SC common-normal projection along branch-switching local arrays.

soundness_flags.label: def:restriction-maps; lem:tangent-normal-form; thm:union-envelope
soundness_flags.one_line: q_PT,x compares donor changes only and has dimension J-1, whereas ass:parallel-trends equates the treated-group change with every donor (J restrictions); thus q_PT does not define the stated PT model and the asserted PT tangent normal form, QP, and envelope do not follow from their dependencies.

soundness_flags.label: symbol E and oeq:uniform-attainment
soundness_flags.one_line: E_P is defined as integration under P_O but is applied to unobserved potential outcomes, and phi_U(P_n) is only defined as an intersection of branch influence classes even when a branch-switching P_n lies outside one branch; a full-data expectation and an explicit off-intersection/local-chart score extension are required.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:union-envelope and oeq:uniform-attainment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The project excludes vanishing overlap, SC rank failure, changing support, covariance degeneracy, and weak-identification asymptotics.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All efficiency and prospective inference claims are conditional on the displayed fixed-interiority, fixed-rank, spectral-gap, and variance-margin regime.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 2.1--2.3, especially Assumptions PDS/PT/SC and equations (1)--(3), lines 104--123 and 149--160; Theorems 2--4, lines 240--354
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes iid panel sampling, defines PT as equality of the treated and each control group's final change conditional on X, defines SC as a common weighted mean path, and supplies separate PT and SC asymptotic conditions plus bootstrap validity under either branch.

The paper characterizes overidentified DiD moment restrictions and derives a closed-form semiparametric efficient influence function and efficiency bound under parallel trends; its displayed Theorem 3.1 is for the two-treatment-group setting.

The article derives panel-DiD ATT semiparametric efficiency bounds under conditional parallel trends and describes the corresponding efficient influence function, making the proposed J=1 reduction a calibration rather than a novel independent result.

The paper studies a semiparametric conditional odds-ratio union model and states that, with finite support for either outcome, its estimators are semiparametrically efficient in the union model at the intersection submodel.
The paper develops cross-fit estimators and fast remainder rates for average linear functionals of conditional expectations, not a branch-switching union-normal projection problem.

The paper studies doubly robust inference in partially linear regression and explicitly notes possible nonregularity when only one nuisance is consistently estimated; it does not supply PT--SC union-projection inference.

The cited study exists and uses a two-way-fixed-effects difference-in-differences comparison of taxed and comparison restaurants; it is a plausible application domain but does not itself establish the proposed efficiency result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace q_PT,x by treated-versus-donor final-change restrictions (and its correct dimension), then rederive the PT tangent space, branch influence class, QP, witness, and J=1 reduction from that corrected model.

Define a full-data expectation separately from the observed-law expectation, and specify a valid local extension of the common score along PT-only and SC-only alternatives before retaining the uniform branch-switching OEQ.

Turn the oracle-adaptation corollary into an actually observable finite-dimensional criterion by writing its Gram-matrix/normal-coefficient test, rather than leaving it as equality or membership of abstract influence classes.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: repair the PT restriction geometry and off-intersection score definition, then re-audit the envelope and witness before advancing to Stage 0.
